scope: Game Math PART2 / 3D Rotations 8.1 through 8.2.5; script and visual instructions only
reviewBasis: Read the full draft once, then reread final changes in m03, m06, m08 and m12, including the final eight-paragraph m06 ordering and its unchanged visual instructions.
Read the supplied Notion article's full selected 8.1-8.2.5 scope, including its correction callouts, in the existing local source record.
Cross-check mathematical convention and technical corrections against primary sources; no source video, new TTS or render was produced.
Execute direct arithmetic and matrix computations for the small worked examples, not a test that merely mirrors generated output.

convention.coordinates: Left-handed pedagogical frame, +X east/right, +Y up, +Z north/forward; positive Y quarter-turn sends forward +Z to +X.
convention.vectorConvention: Row vectors multiplied by the matrix on the right.
convention.RDefinition: vU = vO * R; rows are object/input axes in upright/output coordinates.
convention.directionCosines: R_ij = inputAxis_i dot outputAxis_j, with both geometric axes expressed in one common orthonormal frame.
convention.upright: Auxiliary frame with object origin and world-parallel axes, introduced as terminology used here.
convention.frameInterpretation: Coordinate re-expression does not cause an additional physical movement.
convention.matrixStorage: Row/column vector multiplication convention is distinct from memory row/column-major storage.

claimsReviewed.claim: Direction versus full orientation, reference/home orientation, state versus angular displacement, attitude, fixed-target camera twist, three orientation degrees of freedom.
Unit mutually perpendicular body axes; shared-origin upright frame; object axes in external coordinates; numeric row-matrix construction and fixed-point coordinate conversion.

Transpose equals inverse under orthogonality, scale counterexample, explicit source/destination interface, generic versus dedicated transform representation, 3x3/4x4/row-vector 4x3 affine distinctions.
Dot product and signed projection, cos60=1/2, corrected DCM row/column direction, shared-frame condition, input-frame then output-frame interpretation, row-vector versus column-vector convention.
Direct vector conversion, graphics matrices as common practice without mandatory API exclusivity, space-chain composition, same-axis two-quarter-turn example, inverse order.
15 parts x 15 samples/s; float32=4 bytes; 8100 versus 2700 bytes/s; 162000-byte 30-second difference; uncompressed orientation-only assumptions and distinction from output fps.

Six continuous orthonormality constraints plus determinant-sign restriction, reflections, scale/shear counterexamples, external data versus convention errors, rounding/matrix creep, normalization versus orthonormalization.
Summary remains within 8.2.5; no Euler/gimbal/axis-angle/quaternion lesson added.

sourceCorrectionsVerified.correction: Use vertical Y axis in the chosen Y-up convention rather than the source example's Z.
Use the supplied correction callout's row-vector DCM, consistent with 8.2 and 8.2.5, instead of the transposed 8.2.2 original.
8100 and 2700 are per second, not per animation frame.
Do not claim other rotation representations require explicit matrix conversion before rotating a vector.
Matrices are widely used in conventional graphics transforms; programmable APIs do not require every rotation to be implemented using a matrix.

resolvedNotes.initialConcern: A convention mismatch was placed next to sources of orthogonality damage, which could imply that transposing a valid rotation matrix makes it nonorthogonal.
resolvedNotes.resolution: Final draft explicitly separates measured/file conversion errors that damage axis conditions from convention misreading that can yield an unintended orientation despite valid axis conditions.
Upright is explicitly introduced as this lesson's auxiliary frame terminology.
Input-frame then output-frame interpretation follows the article order while preserving the corrected formula.

primarySources.use: Source teaching logic and source-error locations; the source itself contains the noted DCM and memory-unit errors.
Definition and limited terminology status of upright space.
Orthonormal constraints, determinant +1, transpose inverse and composition. This source uses column vectors; transposed to the selected row-vector convention, with handedness treated consistently.
Quaternion-vector rotation exists without requiring the user to construct an explicit matrix.
Model, view and projection matrices are standard available rendering transforms.
Programmable vertex output gl_Position is used by subsequent coordinate processing; the specification does not mandate matrix-based computation of every object rotation.
